The agency believes that the use of an additional 10 pounds of plastic and an additional 10 pounds of aluminum per vehicle as part of a weight reduction program for General Motors is likely to result from the AFES.

This results in a total increase in each of 5.26 million pounds which is 0.055 percent of the national consumption of aluminum and 0.025 percent of the national consumption of plastics.
The above impacts on natural resources were based on a scenario that assumed for a fleet of vehicles, a ten percent shift in vehicle inertia weight class (see the EPA regulation, Revised Light Duty Truck Regulations for 1979 and Later Model Year Vehicles - 40 FR 56316,

December 28, 1976 for definition of inertia weight) for a 50 pound reduction in vehicle weight for each vehicle. Since only 10 percent of the vehicles shift intertia weight class, the 50 pound weight reduction could be applied to only those vehicles which would shift classes.
